meta.title: How to Put a Quran Verse on Your iPhone Lock Screen
meta.description: A step-by-step guide to showing a daily Quran verse on your iPhone lock screen using widgets, wallpapers, and iOS Focus modes. Lock Screen widgets need iOS 16 or later.

sections.text: To put a Quran verse on your iPhone lock screen, add a Quran lock-screen widget or set a verse wallpaper, then pair it with an iOS Focus mode so it appears automatically. You need an iPhone running iOS 16 or later for Lock Screen widgets and Focus lock screens. An app like [QuranWall](/) places the ayah for you, so you don't have to export, crop, or re-set an image by hand.
Why the lock screen is the best place for Quran

Most of us check our phones dozens of times a day. The lock screen is the one surface you see every single time, before any app, notification, or feed. Putting a verse there means the first thing you read is the Quran, not a red badge. You are not relying on willpower to open another app. The reminder simply meets you where you already are.
And remind, for indeed, the reminder benefits the believers.
What you need before you start

items: An iPhone running **iOS 16 or later** (lock-screen widgets and per-screen wallpapers arrived in iOS 16).
The **QuranWall** app (free to download, with an in-app subscription) for the automatic method, or a saved verse image if you want to do it by hand.
Access to your lock-screen editor: touch and hold your lock screen to open it.

sections.text: Method 1: Add a Quran lock-screen widget (recommended)
A lock-screen widget shows a fresh verse each day, updates on its own, and sits quietly below or above the clock. This is the lowest-effort way to keep Quran in front of you.

items: Download **QuranWall** from the App Store and open it.
Choose your translation language, background, font and colours.
Touch and hold your lock screen, tap **Customize**, then select **Lock Screen**.
Tap the widget area under the clock and add the **QuranWall** widget.
Tap **Done**. A new verse now appears on your lock screen each day.

sections.content: iOS offers inline lock-screen widgets above the clock and rectangular ones below it. Choose whichever shape QuranWall offers that suits the verse length you want to see.

sections.text: Method 2: Set a verse wallpaper with a Focus mode

The wallpaper method puts the verse front and center, and pairing it with a Focus mode makes it appear at the right times while quieting notifications. This is the move if you want a calmer phone during prayer, study, or before bed.

items: In QuranWall, set up the verse wallpaper you like.
Open **Settings > Focus** and create a Focus such as **Quiet Time** or **Prayer**.
Under that Focus, tap **Customize** on the lock screen and choose your QuranWall wallpaper.
Give the Focus a schedule, for example your morning routine or the minutes before each prayer, so the verse appears on its own.

sections.content: Pairing a verse wallpaper with a Focus turns Quiet Time into a one-tap retreat: the Quran fills your screen and the notifications step back.

sections.text: Widget or wallpaper, which should you choose?

items: **Widget** is best for a fresh verse every day with almost no effort. It shows a new ayah each day and stays out of your way.
**Wallpaper with Focus** is best when you want a calmer phone at set times, with the verse taking the whole screen.
**Both** works well too: run a verse wallpaper inside a Quiet Time Focus and keep the widget on your everyday lock screen.

sections.text: Troubleshooting: verse not updating or showing

items: Confirm your iPhone is on **iOS 16 or later** in Settings > General > Software Update.
If a widget is blank, remove it and add it again from the lock-screen editor.
If a wallpaper will not switch, check that the matching Focus is active and linked to that lock screen.
Confirm the widget is added to the lock screen you are actually using, not a different one.

sections.text: Frequently asked questions
Do I need to jailbreak or use Shortcuts?
No. Lock-screen widgets and wallpapers are built into iOS 16 and later, so no jailbreak is involved, and the steps above use no Shortcuts automation.
Is it free?
The download is free; Premium is a subscription, shown in the App Store before you pay.
Will it drain my battery?
Lock-screen widgets and wallpapers are standard iOS features, and iOS decides when a widget refreshes. A verse that changes once a day does not need frequent updates.
Does it work on iPad or Android?
This guide is for iPhone, and QuranWall is an iPhone app with no Android version. iPad handles lock screens differently, so these steps do not apply there.

sections.title: The short version
sections.content: Put a Quran verse on your iPhone lock screen in two ways: add a **QuranWall widget** for a fresh verse every day, or set a **verse wallpaper inside a Focus mode** for a calmer phone at set times. Both need iOS 16 or later for the Lock Screen features.

sections.text: QuranWall is built by [Karol Billik](/about/karol-billik), an indie iOS maker, around one idea: carry the Quran onto the most-seen surface of your phone instead of asking you to remember another app.
